item.title: Billionaire wins appeal overturning A$23.4 million tax bill tied to Tasmania's Woolnorth dairy estate
item.description: A Full Court in Tasmania has overturned a significant tax assessment against companies related to Xianfeng Lu. The decision cancels a A$23.4 million stamp duty bill that included penalties and interest. This dispute originated from the 2016 purchase of the Woolnorth dairy estate, bought for A$280 million. The ruling removes a major financial liability for the companies managing the property in north-west Tasmania.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Shreveport's former Libbey Glass plant faces demolition, with 95% of materials set for recycling
item.description: Full-scale demolition of the former Libbey Glass plant in Shreveport is now underway and progressing. Environmental contaminants have been cleared over the 54-acre site, allowing for redevelopment opportunities. Demolition teams are set to dismantle the industrial silos that have dominated the skyline for decades. Local authorities expect increased truck traffic around Jewella Avenue until mid-2027 due to construction activities.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Iowa farmer turns to solar leases paying $1,200 per acre as falling crop prices squeeze profits
item.description: Tom Green, an Iowa farmer, backs the Folsom Lake Solar Project after it secured the green light from the Mills County Zoning Board. This initiative is set to ensure reliable income through long-term land leases amid tough farming conditions. It promises to produce a substantial amount of electricity, enough to power many local homes, while also creating jobs and boosting tax revenues.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: RHOP star Mia Thornton faces felony theft charge over alleged $11,000 Atlanta condo furniture removal
item.description: Former The Real Housewives of Potomac star Mia Thornton faces a felony theft-by-taking charge over allegations that she and Jared McGriff removed furniture and a television worth approximately $11,000 from a furnished Atlanta condo in October 2025. The case follows Thornton’s November airport arrest over an outstanding larceny warrant. The allegations remain unresolved in court.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Nevada’s ‘lost’ species raise extinction fears as new journal tracks missing plants and animals
item.description: Nevada’s missing plants and animals are drawing attention as a new journal tracks species that have gone undocumented for decades. The concern comes amid a 38% decline in staffing at the state’s US wildlife agency. Globally, more than 4,300 species have not been documented for over a decade, raising questions about conservation and extinction risks.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: George Washington’s childhood home nearly became a Walmart; locals raised $2.2 million to save it
item.description: George Washington spent much of his childhood at Ferry Farm in Virginia, which Walmart purchased in 1996 to build a Supercenter. Residents rallied to save the historic property, raising $2.2 million to buy it back before donating it to a nonprofit foundation. Today, the site features a reconstructed childhood home and interactive historical exhibits for visitors.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Noah’s Ark mystery: 3D-printed model created of Turkey’s 157-metre formation after deep drilling
item.description: Researchers investigating Turkey’s boat-shaped Durupınar formation, believed by some to be Noah’s Ark, have created a 3D-printed model using ground-penetrating radar data. The team has completed its first investigation phase, drilling more than 60 feet underground and collecting samples for laboratory testing. However, many geologists maintain that the formation is a natural geological feature.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Arizona Indigenous sacred site, 6,500 years old, damaged by Trump administration’s border wall
item.description: A 6,500-year-old Indigenous sacred site in Arizona has been damaged during construction of the Trump administration’s border wall. A roughly 50-foot-wide corridor cuts through part of a 272-foot-long geoglyph in the Cabeza Prieta National Wildlife Refuge. The ancient figure predates Egypt’s first pyramid by around 2,000 years, raising concerns over the loss of Indigenous cultural heritage.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Woman spends $380,000 to move her great-great-grandparents’ house to her husband’s family farm
item.description: JaSondra Schmidt and her husband Jason are restoring a historic house from her great-great-grandfather. They decided to relocate the house to their purchased farmland in North Dakota. The family home, built in 1914, carries five generations of JaSondra’s family history. After overcoming several setbacks, they finally acquired the house through a family agreement. The couple is committed to preserving their family legacies through this renovation project.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A couple started a coffee cart using a credit card limit; it now generates $4.5 million a year
item.description: Audrey Finocchiaro and Sam Lancaster founded The Nitro Bar in 2016, embarking on a path marked by financial constraints and initial customer engagement hurdles. Their persistence paid off at Brown University, resulting in significant sales growth. With the help of investors, they expanded into wholesale and retail sectors, achieving impressive annual earnings of $4.5 million and creating 80 jobs.

item.title: Robot sexually assaults 16-year old girl in Germany; 2 teens under probe
item.description: A teenage girl was allegedly groped by a humanoid robot while she was with friends. The incident occurred outside a fast-food restaurant in Cologne shortly after midnight. Police are investigating two young men believed to have recorded and livestreamed the event on social media. The robot, resembling Marvel's Iron Man, was discovered in a Volkswagen by authorities. Investigations are ongoing to determine the individuals responsible for controlling the robot.

item.title: Albania police use tear gas on protesting students as stir turns violent
item.description: In Albania, student protests escalated into violent clashes with police in the capital, Tirana. These demonstrations aimed to highlight critical issues surrounding education and socio-economic challenges. Students raised urgent concerns over campus conditions, rising tuition fees, and uncertain job prospects. Deputy Prime Minister Albana Koçiu denounced the unrest, advocating for peaceful expression. This incident reflects a wider wave of student activism sweeping across Europe, demanding systemic change.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: In 2008, Michael Phelps used his $1 million Olympic bonus to start a foundation; by 2020, it had reached 100,000+ young people
item.description: Michael Phelps, after winning eight gold medals at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, established the Michael Phelps Foundation. This foundation focuses on promoting swimming, water safety, and healthy living for young people. Programs like 'im' aim to instill confidence and coping skills among children. The foundation has expanded to include mental health education during the COVID-19 pandemic. Partnerships with organizations ensure these programs reach diverse communities across the globe.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: He paid $50 for a chair that later sold for $107,950
item.description: Justin Miller, a home design content creator, purchased a chair from Facebook Marketplace for $50. After researching, he discovered it was a rare piece made by Frits Henningsen. Sotheby’s auctioned the chair, which was restored and had an estimated value of $30,000 to $50,000. The auction saw the chair sell for an impressive total of $107,950 including premiums. Miller continues to seek valuable items on platforms like Facebook Marketplace.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: $2 photo of Billy the Kid valued at $5M
item.description: Randy Guijarro discovered an old photograph believed to include Billy the Kid in 2010, purchased for just $2. This photograph has been appraised at $5 million and may confirm its authenticity. After extensive research, experts linked the image to Billy the Kid’s social life during the late summer of 1878. The image also represents a more human side of the infamous outlaw.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Koos Bekker’s company controls 2,700 acres in Somerset, employs 650 locals as expansion sparks debate
item.description: In 2013, Koos Bekker's acquisition of Hadspen House sparked a transformative expansion into The Newt in Somerset, encompassing over 2,700 acres. This growth has generated local employment and attracted visitors, yet opinions remain divided. Many residents welcome the job opportunities, while others voice concerns about the estate's impact on community identity, land stewardship, and environmental sustainability, illustrating the complexity of fostering development without compromising local values.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
